items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing a juvenile sexting and cyberbullying education demonstration program; and providing for the repeal of certain provisions upon the expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5253

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing a juvenile
sexting and cyberbullying education demonstration program; and providing
for the repeal of certain
provisions upon the expiration thereof

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
Directs the attorney general to
establish a 2 year juvenile sexting and cyberbullying education
demonstration program.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section 1. Amends the executive law to add a new section 75 which
requires that the Attorney General, in cooperation with the office of
court administration, establish and implement sexting and
cyberbullying education demonstration programs not less than three
counties throughout the state. The section provides for consultation
with certain entities, and rules and regulations regarding hearing
authorities. The section provides criteria for admission to the
program, components of the instruction given to participating
individuals, and avenues of referrals to the program.

Section 2. Reporting requirements for the Attorney General.

Section 3. Effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Recent headlines have highlighted the unfortunate and significant
consequences of the growing epidemics of cyberbullying and sexting
within our society, particularly among our youth. Both issues focus
on the instantaneous nature of technology, and the responsibilities
that accompany such a privilege.

According to recent studies, cyberbullying has increased in current
years. In nationally representative surveys of 10-17 year olds, twice
as many children and youth indicated that they had been victims and
perpetrators of online harassment in 2005 compared with 1999/2000
(Wolak, Mitchell, & Fickelhor, 2006). Such statistics, coupled with
recent events that have highlighted the negative impacts of
cyberbullying, including effects on school performance, emotional
disturbance, and even death, require immediate intervention.
Nevertheless, the nature of cyberbullying makes the behavior
difficult to see and difficult to correct. In a telephone survey of
preteens (6-11 year olds) and teens (12-17 year olds), 45% of
preteens and 30% of teens who had been cyber-bullied received the
messages while at school, 44% of preteens and
70% of teens who had been cyber-bullied received the messages at home,
and 34% of preteens and 25% of teens who had been cyber-bullied
received the messages while at a friend's house (Fight Crime: Invest
in Kids, 2006). Given the variability of locations, and ease with
which these acts can be committed, we cannot depend on one aspect of
the child's environment to remedy bullying. As such, this bill will


create a pilot program that will work in collaboration with community
groups, authorizing schools, police departments, and any other
entities deemed appropriate by the Attorney General to create a
comprehensive reporting mechanism for cyberbullying and sexting.

"Sexting," a colloquial term for sending nude or obscene photographs
through electronic technologies, has not only been adopted as a new
word in our society, but has become a new health concern and form of
teenage bullying that requires immediate attention and must be
recognized in our societal consciousness. Sexting can result in
damage to one's reputation, depression, and in some cases, suicide.
Alternatively, sexting can also lead to the inadvertent violation of
civil and criminal laws. Given the serious nature of such offenses,
including possible violations of child pornography laws, a
diversionary program will create an avenue whereby juveniles will be
educated on the nature of the behavior without receiving a criminal
record given certain conditions.

In light of the serious nature of both cyberbullying and sexting, acts
that rise above the level of an ordinary problem in society, this
legislation creates a program of education and diversion from
already existing criminal laws and possible family court proceedings
that can and have been applied to such behavior. While sexting and
cyberbullying are not currently defined as crimes under state law,
and this bill does not do so, in the event the acts of either are
viewed to constitute a crime under existing law, this proposal would
not exempt such acts from the criminal law.

This bill will create a two year pilot program in the Attorney
General's office, in conjunction with the Office of Court
Administration, to educate the youth of our State about the
consequences of cyberbullying and sexting. The diversionary program
will focus on the legal consequences of such actions, the non-legal
consequences of such actions including the effect on relationships and
loss of educational and employment opportunities, and the long-term
effects of such behavior. Diversion programs for sexting and
cyberbullying have been used in states including Florida, Ohio, and
Vermont.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect January 1, 2012 and section one of the act
shall expire and be deemed repealed January 1, 2014. Provided, that
effective immediately, any actions necessary to implement the
provisions of section 75 of the executive law, as added by section
one of this act, on its effective date are authorized and directed to
be completed on or before such date.

A.lawCode: Add §423-b, Soc Serv L; add §530.15, CP L; add §303.4, Fam Ct Act
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5253A

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the social services law, in relation to creating an
educational reform
program for certain offenders who are criminally charged with certain
offenses
involving the creation, exhibition or distribution of a photograph
depicting nudity
through the use of an electronic communication device, an interactive
wireless
communications device or a computer; and to amend the criminal
procedure law and
the family court act, in relation to creating a diversionary program
for cases involving
certain offenders who are criminally charged with certain offenses
involving the
creation, exhibition or distribution of a photograph depicting nudity
through the use
of an electronic communication device, an interactive wireless
communications
device or a computer

PURPOSE:
The Cyber-Crime Youth Rescue Act, will create a Diversionary
Program and an Educational Reform Program as an alternative to
prosecution for juveniles charged with offenses involving sexually
explicit photographs through the use of an electronic communication
device, an interactive wireless communications device, or through the
use of a computer.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
The social services law is amended to add a new
section 423(b) authorizing and requiring the OFCS in consultation
with the chief administrator of the courts and the commissioner of
the Department of Education to develop and implement Educational
Reform Program (hereafter "ERP") for eligible offenders referred to
the ERP. This section explains the structure, purpose, function, and
operation of the ERP.

The criminal procedure law is amended by to add a new section 530.15
that establishes the Divisionary Program. This section requires that
an eligible offender charged with an eligible offense be diverted to
the ERP. This section establishes conditions for diversion, defines
eligible offenders and eligible offenses and further defines ERP.

The family court act is amended to add a new section 303.4 which
applies provisions of the new section 530.15 of criminal procedure
law to any proceedings in family court that involves an eligible
offender and eligible offense.

JUSTIFICATION:
The dangerous combination of teenagers behaving
provocatively and impulsively is not new, but easy accessibility to


the technology is. With cell phone cameras, teenagers have been
handed a tool so easy to use, that for some it's impossible to pass up.

This, mostly teenage practice of sexting and posting sexual images
online is a nationwide problem that has perplexed parents, school
administrators, and law enforcement officials. Prosecutors in several
states have charged teenagers, who have texted photographs of
themselves, or their friends, or partners with distribution of child
pornography.

Currently, under New York State law, sexting can result in felony
charges including creating, possession, and distribution of child
pornography regardless of the age of the offender, the intent of the
offender and the circumstances surrounding the distribution of the
information. While some local police and prosecutors have used
discretion to spare youth and their families the trauma of criminal
prosecution, current New York law does not provide for a formal
alternative to criminal prosecution. Thus, an offending youth, for a
single youthful indiscretion could be subject to severe criminal
consequences that could. have permanent negative effects that last a
lifetime.

This bill establishes a Diversionary Program and an Educational Reform
Program as an alternative to prosecution for certain juveniles who are
charged with a criminal offense for posting sexually suggestive or
sexually explicit photographs, or who engage in the behavior commonly
known as sexting, in which these pictures are transmitted via cell
phones or other electronic devices.

The educational reform program would focus on legal consequences of
transmitting explicit photos as well as non-legal consequences, such
as the effect on relationships and the loss of job opportunities.
Also covered would be the unique nature of cyberspace, whose infinite
audience can create unforeseen, long-term consequences for sharing of
sexually explicit materials, and the link between bullying and
sharing of explicit materials. The program will educate the offending
youth on the legal and non-legal consequences of sharing sexually
suggestive or explicit materials and any
such sanctions that might accompany such behavior as well as
emphasizing the connections between sexting, and cyber-bullying.

Upon the completion of the program, the youth will have an opportunity
to possibly avoid prosecution by application to the Court for
dismissal of the charges. The Court can dismiss the charges after
careful consideration of all relevant materials. The youth will then
have a chance to continue a productive life without having incurred a
criminal record.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
None.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Undetermined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the hundred eighth day
after it shall become law; provided that, effective immediately, the


commissioner of the office of children and family services, the
commissioner of the department of education and the chief
administrator of the courts shall promulgate any rules and regulations
and take all other actions necessary to implement the provisions of
this act on our before its effective date.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5253B

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the social services law, the family court act and the penal
law, in relation to creating an
education reform
program for certain individuals
charged with certain
offenses
involving the creation, exhibition or distribution of a photograph
depicting nudity
through the use of an electronic communication device, an interactive
wireless
communications device or a computer

PURPOSE:
The Cyber-Crime Youth Rescue Act, will create an Educational
Program that will address the specific issues facing youth that
commit these types of offenses

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. States that this act shall be known and may be cited as
"the cyber-crime youth rescue act".

Section 2. Adds a new section to the social services law which shall
create and implement an education reform program for persons who
commit certain offenses.

Section 3. Amends the Family Court Act to include this new program as
a condition that may be imposed pursuant to granting an adjournment
in contemplation of dismissal at the outset of the case.

Section 4. Amends the Family Court Act to include this new program as
a condition that may be imposed pursuant to granting an adjournment
in contemplation of dismissal after the fact finding stage of the case.

Section 5. Amends the Family Court Act to include this new program as
an option for diversion in the case of a person in need of
supervision (PINS).

Section 6. Adds a new section to the penal law to include this new
program as a condition that may be imposed pursuant to a conditional
discharge.

JUSTIFICATION:
The dangerous combination of teenagers behaving
provocatively and impulsively is not new, but easy accessibility to
the technology is with cell phone cameras, teenagers have been
handed a tool so easy to use, that for some it's impossible to pass up.

This, mostly teenage practice of sexting and posting sexual images
online is a nationwide problem that has perplexed parents, school
administrators, and law enforcement officials. Prosecutors in several
states have charged teenagers, who have texted photographs of


themselves, or their friends, or partners with distribution of child
pornography.

While this bill does not change the penalties that may be imposed for
committing these types of offenses, it does add a newly developed
education program for eligible persons, the court may order such
persons to attend and complete this program which is tailored to
address the prevention of these offenses in the future.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
None.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Undetermined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the hundred eighth day
after it shall become law; provided that, effective immediately, the
commissioner of the office of children and family services shall
promulgate any rules and regulations and take all other actions
necessary to implement the provisions of this act on our before its
affective date.

summary: Creates an educational reform program and a diversionary program for certain juveniles who are criminally charged with certain offenses involving the creation, exhibition or distribution of a photograph depicting nudity through the use of an electronic communication device, an interactive wireless communications device or a computer.
title: Creates an educational reform program and a diversionary program for juveniles who are charged with offenses involving a photograph depicting nudity
